spf_all_resolution_is_ok.description: An include: or redirect= target that does not exist, has no SPF record, has several records or a broken one makes receivers return permerror once evaluation reaches it. a, mx and exists names that return no records never match (void lookups; more than two make the record permerror). A temporary DNS failure makes receivers return temperror.
spf_all_resolution_is_ok.fix: Every include: and redirect= target must publish exactly one valid SPF record. Check the target name against your provider's current documentation — providers rename and retire these names — fix the target's record if it is yours, or remove the term.
spf_all_resolution_is_ok.resultText: Some terms point to names that do not resolve, or to include/redirect targets without a valid SPF record.
spf_all_resolution_is_ok.title: Mechanism resolution check
spf_all_resolution_is_ok.value: include:_spf.wpengine.com has no SPF record (none). Receivers that reach this include return permerror (RFC 7208 §5.2)

spf_no_duplicate_include_found.description: Including the same domain twice — in two include: terms, or in include: and redirect= — spends another of the 10 allowed DNS lookups without adding any sender.
spf_no_duplicate_include_found.fix: Remove duplicate include: terms: each extra copy spends another DNS lookup and adds no sender. If the duplicate is inside a provider's record you include, the provider already covers it, so remove your own include — unless the outer include is the provider's corporate or umbrella record (for example include:salesforce.com) that authorizes more than you use: then keep the include the provider documents for customers (include:_spf.salesforce.com) and remove the umbrella one. If the provider's record lists the same domain twice, only the provider can fix that.

spf_number_of_lookups_is_ok.resultText: The number of DNS lookups doesn't exceed the 10-lookup limit.
spf_number_of_lookups_is_ok.title: Number of DNS lookups check

spf_number_of_void_lookups_is_ok.description: A void lookup is a DNS query from an SPF term that returns no records (NXDOMAIN or an empty answer). RFC 7208 §4.6.4 allows at most two; past that, receivers return permerror for every sender not matched before that point. A single void lookup only means the term never matches. Terms whose answer depends on the sender — exists, a or mx with a macro such as %{i}, and ptr — are counted for a sender the record does not list (192.0.2.1): for such a sender they usually return nothing, which is normal, but it counts toward the limit. A ptr term does so only for senders without reverse DNS, so a limit that is reached only with ptr is reported as a notice.
spf_number_of_void_lookups_is_ok.fix: The terms listed in the finding return no records for a sender they do not match, and at the third of them receivers stop with permerror (RFC 7208 §4.6.4): every sender not matched before it fails SPF, including senders listed later in your record. Bring the count under three: remove an include that repeats a record you already include (often a provider's corporate record, such as include:salesforce.com next to the include:_spf.salesforce.com it documents for customers), remove includes of services you no longer use, and fix or remove a, mx or exists terms whose names do not exist. Keep the include each provider documents for customers. Until then, put the ip4:/ip6: terms and includes of your main senders before these terms, so that those senders pass before the limit.
spf_number_of_void_lookups_is_ok.resultText: The number of void lookups exceeds the allowed limit of 2.
spf_number_of_void_lookups_is_ok.title: Number of void lookups check
spf_number_of_void_lookups_is_ok.value: Void lookup limit exceeded: exists:%{i}._spf.mta.salesforce.com (inside _spf.salesforce.com), exists:%{i}._spf.mta.salesforce.com (inside salesforce.com → _spf.salesforce.com) and exists:%{i}._spf.corp.salesforce.com (inside salesforce.com) return no records for a sender they do not match, so receivers return permerror at the 3rd for every sender not matched before it, including senders listed later in the record (RFC 7208 §4.6.4)
